facts.fact: Digital Policy Alert describes Ghana's 2008 Electronic Transactions Act as an existing law that sets fair business practice requirements for suppliers, consumer rights and liability protections for intermediaries.

Digital Policy Alert reports that in November 2023 Ghana's Ministry of Communications and Digitalisation issued an enforcement notice under the Electronic Transactions Act requiring all e-commerce platforms and digital delivery companies to register by January 2024.

slug: 2024-09-20 Ghana Digital Economy (US Country Commercial Guide)

facts.fact: The US Country Commercial Guide, published 2024-09-20, says the 2008 Electronic Transactions Act is Ghana's e-commerce and e-signature baseline.
The op-ed names the Electronic Transactions Act as part of Ghana's existing legal foundation.
The article describes the Electronic Transactions Act, 2008 (Act 772) as ensuring safety in electronic transactions including mobile money, and criminalising mobile wallet hacking and identity fraud.

note: No rules made under it or application stated.

facts.fact: The document names the Electronic Transactions Act, 2008 (Act 772) as a law under which NITA is mandated as national IT regulator, speaking of it as existing law.

note: Carnegie lists the NITA agency act and an AI strategy; neither is this study's law.
UNCTAD lists the Electronic Transactions Act, 2008; already held as GHA-001.
